inputs.text: Tens of thousands marched in central London under the banner of opposing the “far-right,” with trade unions, anti-racism groups and Muslim representative bodies among the organisers. With local elections approaching, this looks less like a neutral show of civic concern and more like organised pressure to define which views are acceptable. Calling people “far-right” is an easy way to dismiss concerns about national identity, social order and cultural continuity instead of answering them. Tradition and public debate deserve better than political labels.
